correctness.rationale: For each ideal vertex a deep cusp is exactly Q×[z0,∞) with hyperbolic density z^-3. The exact elementary polygon erosion A−A_t=Lt−(Σ cot(θ/2))t² holds up to the first edge disappearance, and z^-3 integration of z²sinh²(s) gives the logarithm. Above the cutoff the integral is O(s²), while the compact truncated piece gives total face area s+O(s²). Each edge is represented by exactly two ideal vertex figures, and Gauss–Bonnet/Euler gives total face area 2π(v−2). Normalization uses V. The ideal tetrahedron Jensen inequality and strictly concave Lobachevsky sum prove unique regular equality. Independent polygon-clipping/finite-cusp quadrature checker ran successfully; computations only corroborate, not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The entire nontrivial natural class of finite-sided convex ideal hyperbolic three-polyhedra has finite face area and infinite edge lengths, so classical compact polyhedron second-order inner-tube edge terms fail. The theorem determines the replacement s² log(1/s) term with intrinsic dihedral coefficient, including a sharp regular ideal tetrahedron extremal. The coefficient is a geometric invariant with potential use in geometric probability, cusp asymptotics and comparison of ideal polyhedron shapes, not a routine finite example.
